FOREWORD 

This Indian Standard was adopted by the Bureau of Indian Standards on 24 May 1989, after the 
draft finalized by the Forestry and Plantation Machinery Sectional Camm^tee i^ fe^n approved 
by the Agricultural and Food Products Division Council, 

Wooden jointers are used for jointing of bow sav/ blades as per IS 11251 : 1985 ^Specification for 
bow saw blades', A used worn out flat file shall be fitted by the user before using these wooden 
jointers. The flat file shall be of 150 mm length, 11 mm width and 2*2 mm thickness and shall have 
22 cuts per centimetre. This used file may be supplied by the manufacturer at the option of the 
purchaser. 

Jointing is done to bring all the teeth of bow saw blade in a line so that all teeth are taking part 
in the cutting action. _The jointing is done by placing the file overthe top of the jointer and then 
pushing it forward. The jointing stroke shall touch all the teeth. Since the blade wears out most 
heavily in the middle, extra filing stroke may be needed at the ends of the blades. 

In the preparation of this standard, assistance has been derived from the Forest Operations 
Division, Forest Research Institute (ICFR), Dehra Dun. 

For the purpose of deciding whether a particular requirement of this standard is complied with, 
the final value, observed or calculated, expressing the result of a test or analysis, shall be rounded 
off in accordance with IS 2 : i960 'Rules for rounding oif numerical \alues ( revised )\ The 
number of significant places retained in the rounded off value should be the same as that of specifi- 
ed value in the standard. 



IS 12704 : 1989 



Indian Standard 



FORESTRY TOOLS - WOODEN JOINTER FOR 
BOW SAW BLADE - SPECIFICATION 



1 SCOPE 

1.1 This standard specifies the material, dimen- 
sions and otiier requirements of wooden jointer 
used fot jointing of bow saw blades as per 
IS 11251 : 1985, 'Specification for bow saw 
blades'. 

2 REFERENCES 

The following Indian Standards are necessary 
adjuncts to this standard. 



IS No. 

IS 2102 (Part 1) 
1980 



Title 

General tolerances for di- 
mensions and form and 
position : Part 1 General 
tolerances for linear and 
angular dimensions {second 
revision ) 

IS 4905 : 1968 Methods for random sam- 

pling 

3 MATERIAL 

3.1 Wooden jointers shall be made from good 
quality properly seasoned carpentry wood. 

3.2 The wooden blanks shall be free from centre 
heart ( pith ), decay ( rot ), checks, shakes, 
splits, borer holes, warp, etc. 

4 SHAPE AND DIMENSIONS 

4.1 The shape and dimensions shall be as given 
in Fig. 1. 

4,1*1 Tolerances for various dimensions shall 
be very coarse class specified in IS 2102 
( Part 1 ) : 1980. 



4.2 A used flat file ( see Foreword for the di- 
mensions of the flat file ) shall be fitted by the 
user before performing the jointing operation 
with the wooden jointer. 

5 WORKMANSHIP AND FINISH 

5.1 The wooden jointer shall be smooth finished 
and shall be free from burrs, sharp edges, cracks 
and other defects. 

5.1.1 It is recommended that immediately after 
manufacture, wooden jointers shall be dipped in 
raw linseed oil at about 90°C for one hour, 

6 DESIGNATION 

6.1 The wooden jointer shall be designated by 
its name and the Indian Standard number as: 

Wooden Jointer IS 12704. 

7 MARKING 

7.1 Each wooden jointer shall be clearly and 
legibly stamped with the manufacturer's name 
or trade mark^ if any; and the batch or code 
number. 

8 PACKING 

8,1 The packing shall be as agreed to between 
manufacturer and the purchaser. 

9 SAMPLING 

9.1 Unless otherwise agreed to between the 
manufacturer and the purchaser, the sampling 
plan and criteria for conformity shall be as given 
in Annex A.

ANNEX A 
(Clause 9 A ) 
SCALE OF SAMPLING AND CRITERIA FOR CONFORMITY 



Al SCALE OF SAMPLING 

Al.l Lot 

In any consignment, all the wooden jointers of 
the same nominal size manufactured under 
similar conditions of manufacture shall be 
grouped together to constitute a lot. 

A-1.2 For ascertaining the conformity of the 
lot to the requirements of this specification, 
tests shall be carried out on wooden jointers 
selected from each lot separately. The number 
of wooden jointers to be selected at random 
from a lot shall be in accordance with col 1 and 
2 of Table I. To ensure the randomness of 
selection, the procedure as laid down in IS 4905 : 
1968 shall be followed. 

A-2 NUMBER OF TESTS AND CRITERIA 
FOR CONFORMITY 

A-2.1 The wooden jointers selected according 
to A-1.2 shall be examined for material ( see 3 ), 
dimensions { see 4) and general requirements

Standard Mark 

The use of the Standard Mark is governed by the provi&ions of the Bureau of Indian 
Standards Act^ 1986 and the Rules and Regulations made thereunder. The Standard Mark on 
products covered by an Indian Standard conveys the assurance that they have been produced 
to comply with the requirements of that standard under a well defined system of inspection, 
testing and quality control which is devised and supervised by BIS and operated by the pro- 
ducer. Standard marked products are also continuously checked by BIS for conformity to 
that standard as a further safeguard* Details of conditions under which a licence for the use 
of the Standard Mark may be granted to manufacturers or producers may be obtained from 
the Bureau of Indian Standards- 



Bareati of Indian Standards

promote harmonious development of the activities of standardization, marking and quality 
certification of goods and attending to connected matters in the country.
